# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later Q&A)

## BOOK 1 of 2: THE WORLD MASTERS, by George Griffith (1903, John Long; Gutenberg 38028)

**Front matter:** Author's other works: The Angel of the Revolution, Brothers of the Chain, The Justice of Revenge, A Honeymoon in Space, Captain Johnnie. Sidelights on Convict Life (ready shortly). Publisher John Long, 13 & 14 Norris Street, Haymarket, London.

**PROLOGUE "The Moment of Triumph":** Strassburg, night, old Fisher's Gate near River Ill. Dr Emil Fargeau (~60, tall, spare, stooping, iron-grey hair, Alsatian, ex-Prof Physical Science Univ. of Strassburg). Laboratory in attic. Machine: round, ~3 ft, glass cylinder, four glass supports, wooden dish, bright steel plate (4 in square, 1 in thick), circle of needles; two battery sets. Wooden-bird cuckoo clock. He smashes steel with wooden mallet. Speech: will break Germany; France to rule world; "Soul of the World"/Living Principle of Material Things. Adelaide = daughter of Bourbon line; Victor = his son, to marry her. Finances: ten twenty-mark gold pieces + ~25 marks. Jew Weinthal (money-lender) held a draft; Fargeau altered figures.

**CH I (27 Jan, Kaiser's birthday, German Embassy, Nevski Prospekt, St Petersburg):** Prince Louis Xavier de Condé, Duc de Montpensier (~50, Bourbon features, Order of St Vladimir, Golden Fleece, refuses French orders, hates Republic). Daughter Adelaide de Condé, Marquise de Montpensier (<21, beautiful, "Marie Antoinette replica"). Captain Victor Fargeau (~28, Uhlan, military attaché German Embassy). Count Leo Valdemar (Chief Third Section, Ministry of Interior; big, bearded) and daughter Countess Sophie Valdemar (19, fair, pansy-blue eyes, sensuous mouth, "most skilful diplomatic detective in Europe"). Adelaide & Victor walk to winter garden: "Succeeded? ... He goes to Paris to-morrow." Sophie overhears partially. French Ambassador absent (sent attaché, "friction" with Germany). Sophie's friend Sophie-knows-everything.

**CH II:** Fargeau at French Minister of War's office, Paris; refused ("show me the apparatus", "pfennige"). Minister offers 50-franc note; Fargeau demands 1000 francs. Fargeau's Strassburg debts; mortgaged farms. Hotel in Paris; wrote letters: to Victor (Petersburg), to Reuss Weinthal (Judenstrasse, Strassburg), and specifications in air-tight tin case. Took Nord Station → Southampton via le Havre. Midnight, mid-Channel, speech "Tant pis pour toi"; threw himself overboard; screw mangled him; tin box lashed to body.

**CH III:** May morning, steam yacht *Nadine*, between Guernsey & Southampton. Owner Ernest Shafto Hardress, Viscount Branston (eldest son of Earl of Orrel). Guest Frank Lamson, M.A. Cambridge, D.Sc. London (32, cold, bloodless voice). Body sighted by Lamson; stopped with engine telegraph; quarter-boat; mate Mr Jackson. Tin box cut from body. Lady Olive (Orrel's daughter, ~25, Irish eyes); Miss Chrysie Vandel (daughter of Clifford K. Vandel, President American Electrical Storage Trust, Buffalo NY; fair, deep blue eyes, "ever so little too large" mouth). Kipling "Seven Seas" exchange. Yacht speeds to 20 knots.

**CH IV:** Lamson opens box in cabin, locks door, reads, tempted; "Good Lord, is that me?" Hardress brings brandy-soda. Lamson reveals discovery: electrical/magnetic "tides", control of metals/steam; "How would you like to be master of the world?" Hardress eagerly sees millions; Lamson says Vandel would form trust. Hardress: "Let's go and break it gently to the girls."

**CH V:** Orrel Court (Hampshire, South Downs). Dinner: Earl Harry Shafto Hardress, 8th Earl of Orrel (50s); Clifford K. Vandel "Lightning King" (tall, iron-grey moustache, Southern accent). Port; Lamson explains scheme; Vandel: "Masters of the world... I guess we'll do it." Chrysie's remark about "Lord Beaconsfield". Hardress proposes to Chrysie.

**CH VI:** Syndicate = International Magnetic Control Syndicate. Vandel president; Lamson studies US electrical machinery; Hardress leases Boothia Felix (Boothia Land), magnetic pole, from Canadian Govt, £1000/yr for 10 yrs. Hardress proposes to Chrysie at Buffalo ("option on territory"/"seal on contract"/"syllabus"); she won't say yes yet. Vandel accepts Hardress. Prince Condé and Adelaide travel toward Elsenau.

**CH VII:** Elsenau spa (Hôtel Wilhelmshof, Hartz–Thuringia; spring for gout). July. Lord Orrel & Lady Olive on verandah. Prince & Adelaide arrive. Olive & Adelaide friendship. Orrel-Prince friendship (met at Aix-les-Bains 6 yrs before; Orrel's brother died fighting for France 1870-71, murdered by communards). Prince reveals Fargeau's secret.

**CH VIII:** Orrel tells prince the Nadine story; prince collapses in grief ("Mon Dieu... It is the same!"). Prince's madness at night; daughter Adelaide given his opiate; prince dies (broken vessel, cries "France! ... maîtresse du monde"). Resident physician. Hardress arrives from Paris same evening.

**CH IX:** Funeral at Elsenau (brick grave, pines). Aunt Madame de Condé, Princess of Bourbon. Adelaide's secret journal (shorthand-locked volume, silver key); writes of Victor, Hardress ("master of the world"), Lady Olive; "I wonder if there is another woman?"

**CH X:** Lord Orrel & Hardress discuss; Hardress reveals Chrysie. Vienna (Hôtel on Ringstrasse). Adelaide tells Victor of father's death; Victor resigns, going to Paris, reveals father's duplicate papers; plan: French Arctic expedition. Adelaide: "one more woman".

**CH XI:** Victor in Paris (Avenue de l'Opéra hotel); friend Gaston Leraulx (ministry secretary). Adelaide at Avenue Neuilly hotel. Victor resigned; German extradition. Sophie & count call (condolence) — "diplomatists and spies" jab; Sophie reveals Boothia Land lease.

**CH XII:** Sophie & count dine General Ducros (Minister of War) — intelligence via Russian trapper & French-Canadian voyageur's telegrams. Plan: Ducros's private room for eavesdropping. Interview: Victor & Adelaide before Ducros; Victor's scheme: French Arctic expedition with guns, to seize works. Ducros admits mistake. Sophie listens.

**CH XIII:** Cowes week, Orrel Court (later summer). Chrysie confides to father Vandel that Adelaide is rival; Vandel suspects Franco-Russian expeditions aimed at Boothia. Telegram to Lamson in cipher.

**CH XIV:** Sophie & count plan: kidnap Orrels, Vandels, Adelaide etc. with Russian yacht *Vlodoya*; agent Edward Williams (second engineer of Nadine; grudge over patents, seduced by Sophie); Jules (maid's brother); spies. Plot to sabotage Nadine's engines and intercept mid-Atlantic. Chrysie overheard earlier.

**CH XV:** The Storage Works at Boothia (Port Adelaide, Cape Adelaide; tower over magnetic pole; telegraph via Winnipeg; masts). Lamson & Austin Vandel (nephew, general manager). Vandel's cipher telegram; Hardress & Orrel plan crossing to Halifax. Count & Sophie learn of telegram (maid Felice/Jules).

**CH XVI:** Adelaide hears from Victor (expeditions ready; Russian ice-breaker *Ivan the Terrible*). Sophie tells Adelaide of plan. Chrysie & Adelaide talk on lawn; Hardress news: German military scandal (Victor's extradition).

**CH XVII:** Sophie persuades Adelaide to join plot (Adelaide sets condition: no harm to Hardress, Orrels, Vandels, but "the sooner you get them out of the way" re Chrysie). Chrysie sees them together.

**CH XVIII:** Cowes broken up; Nadine sails from Southampton earlier than planned. Telegram intercepted by Felice (copy by Chrysie: "Dépêchez"). Williams sabotage arranged. Vlodoya at Cherbourg.

**CH XIX:** Nadine at full speed (20 knots). Captain Burgess; chief engineer M'Niven; second officer Mr Vernon. Williams summoned, suspected.

**CH XX:** Guns mounted (Vandel's "dynamite gun", Vandelite shell, liquid gas). Williams caught sanding driving rod / gritting shaft. Punch "à le Grand Monarque" drugged. Chrysie's Smith & Wesson revolver.

**CH XXI:** Nadine crippled, speed 8 knots. Punch drugged Hardress, Orrel, Olive, Madame de Bourbon, Adelaide. Captain & M'Niven revive. Vlodoya approaches.

**CH XXII:** Naval duel: Vlodoya disabled (Vandel's shell). Chrysie's Maxim. Count Valdemar & Sophie surrender on bridge; captain of Vlodoya killed.

**CH XXIII:** Vlodoya crew set adrift; coal transferred; Vlodoya sunk. Count & Sophie prisoners on Nadine. Dinner. Nadine heads to Boothia.

**CH XXIV:** Press reports (Globe leader). Germany demands Fargeau extradition; France mobilises; Russia threatens; Kaiser and Europe mobilize. Trust circular (dollar per head capitation, Old Broad Street London; electrical cut-off in one week).

**CH XXV:** Works start (Hardress/Orrel/Vandel; Chrysie pulls lever at 6 o'clock). Dies: French ironclad *Charles Martel* disabled; Brunsbüttel fort gun bursts; Kiel communications dead.

**CH XXVI:** Europe paralysed; starvation; Kaiser & President Loubet arrive England; King Edward mediation. Russian & French expeditions reach Adelaide Bay.

**CH XXVII:** Expeditions anchor 4 miles off; Trust aërograph messages; Adelaide & Sophie plot to shoot Chrysie & Hardress; Sophie gives Adelaide Chrysie's revolver.

**CH XXVIII:** Lamson/Orrel invite Admirals Nazanoff (Russian) and Dumont (French), Victor Fargeau, Prof Josef Karnina to dinner. Telegram from King Edward proposing arbitration (signed "Edward R.I."). Vandel: "frozen that war clean out."

**CH XXIX:** Dinner: Fargeau claims legacy; Hardress refuses surrender; admirals demand decision by six am. Death-ray sites on towers. Lady Olive plays "God Save the King." Shooting at gate: Adelaide shoots Hardress (broken thigh), Chrysie (arm), Sophie & Fargeau shoot back; Lamson's disintegrator ray kills Sophie, Adelaide, Fargeau (to bones).

**CH XXX:** Lord Orrel's warning; admirals depart; Williams handed to them. Count Valdemar vows vengeance; Nazanoff: "Holy Russia". Count to fire first gun.

**CH XXXI:** Dawn assault; count killed by ray at gun (Ivan). Nazanoff & Dumont killed; French & Russian ships destroyed; survivors (Ivan & remnants) return to Europe. Adelaide's and Sophie's remains in caskets sent to Madame de Bourbon and count's brother.

**EPILOGUE:** Hardress & Chrysie recovering; Lamson reports Powers surrendered; arbitration rules; Chrysie: "We four... run the world"; contract kiss.

**Catalogue pages** (John Long): many titles incl. Mrs Lovett Cameron, May Crommelin, etc.

## BOOK 2 of 2: THE CHEVALIER'S DAUGHTER; or, An Exile for the Truth, by Lucy Ellen Guernsey (Gutenberg 73365; Stanton-Corbet Chronicles, year 1660; John F. Shaw & Co.)

**Note (by Rosamond Genevieve Corbet, Tre Madoc Court, 1 May 1740):** memoirs of grandmother Agnes Genevieve Corbet née d'Antin, written in old age. Papers found in carved cabinet.

**Chapter list:** I Early Recollections; II The Tour d'Antin; III Youthful Days; IV Trust and Distrust; V Guests at the Tour; VI The Lonely Grange; VII A Sudden Summons; VIII Flight; IX In Jersey; X To England; XI Tre Madoc; XII Mischief; XIII The Book; XIV A Wedding; XV Stanton Court; XVI London; XVII My New Friends; XVIII A Great Step; XIX Another Change; XX "You shall have no Choice"; XXI The Convent; XXII The Voyage; XXIII Conclusion.

**CH I:** Narrator "Vevette" (Genevieve), born 1660 at Tour d'Antin near Sartilly, Normandy (near Granville, Mont St Michel). Father Chevalier Armand d'Antin (younger son of De Fayrolles family, Provence; Vaudois ancestry). Mother Margaret Corbet (English, Devonshire/Cornwall family; pale, grey eyes, serious, devout; loved English Church). Elder brother Louis de... (uncle Charles, uncle who converted; Marquis de Fayrolles is father's eldest brother; Uncle Charles (Corbet) is mother's brother in London). Foster parents Simon & Jeanne Sablot (farm); children David (foster brother, later ship-carpenter at Dieppe), Lucille "Loulou" (jealous). Servants: Mrs Grace (English, Cornish; ankle, dies later), Julienne, Marie, Mathew, Henri. Dog Hal (mastiff), cat Blanchon (white, never mews). Temple = Protestant meetinghouse. Curé Father Francois (kind, fat). Gilded angel on Mont St Michel. Grève quicksands. Father's hyphen-fights. David runs to Granville procession (St Michael feast, Sunday), Vevette tells; Simon: "Thou must never ... enter a church or bow thy head to any image." Persecution history; Merindol & Cabrières massacre (1540s). Uncle (head of family) converted to curry favor with Louis XIV.

**CH II:** Vevette goes home to Tour d'Antin; the room in corner turret; Mrs Grace (Cornish, prim). Father: "a true Corbet". Father reports: convent at Sartilly reopened (hospital of St Jacques) = danger. Curé's warning about wolves. Vevette learns to spin on wheel from England; David builds spinning-wheel for her birthday. Lucille jealous. Blackberries; apples.

**CH III:** Years of study (Whole Duty of Man, Practice of Piety, Holy Living and Dying). Vevette steals a play (witty, profane); lies; mother's stern anger; Vevette burns others later. Arcadia (Sidney), Faerie Queene (Spenser), Hakluyt's Voyages. Convent of Sartilly epidemic, fire, flood; abandoned. Persecution details. Father's duties as landlord. David apprenticed at Dieppe.

**CH IV:** Late September. Grace's sprained ankle (fell in doorway). Vevette meets Lucille on rock at lane (pale; sulking over "the Religion"); Lucille rebellious ("I hate the very name of the Religion"). Procession of nuns (hospital) with Mère Luchon's grandchildren (Luchon girl ~7 and baby). New curé (thin, sharp, cruel mouth). Father secretly tells Vevette she must guard old pastor Monsieur Bertheau in secret passage in old tower. Secret stall in chapel (fourth stall). Chapel: Spanish altarpiece; music loft organ.

**CH V:** Night: Vevette leads pastor Bertheau (Monsieur Bertheau) through secret passage to top-of-tower room; mastiff Hal. Countersign "The name of the Lord is a strong tower". Lucille apostatizes (kneels to priest, receives gilded crucifix; "I am going to try what holy Mother Church can do for me"); breaks with Vevette. Lucille's note later. Pastor gets milk. Vevette's mother; Mrs Grace's storeroom. Jeanne's note of Lucille's disappearance (silver dove, gold chain left).

**CH VI:** Andrew Corbet (English cousin, ~20, short, broad, large grey eyes, black crisp hair; trained at sea; wholly Protestant). Father-friends. Vevette's destined marriage to Andrew (family compact). Father's plan to flee to England. Night meeting at lonely grange (Jean Martin, Luchon). Pastor Bertheau's communion in vault; false alarm (horses). Pastor leaves; boat capsized in storm; survivor later.

**CH VII:** Andrew's stay; botany. Pilgrimage procession (St Michael feast); Lucille's apostate face. Storm; poor little Luchon and nun drowned. Mrs Grace dies (heart/swoon). Burial in vault under chapel (niche).

**CH VIII:** Secret tunnel discovered by father; Andrew helps. Father's farewell; pilgrims. Priest & mob attack (Michaud, the gamekeeper, saved from galleys by father; now shoots at Andrew's uncle). Father killed (shot by Michaud). Lucille's packet via Pierre Le Febre ("grosse mouche" = bluebottle = "Fly"). Andrew rides back; tower falls (floor trap); Blanchon the cat scares priest; escape by boat (Pierre Le Febre's boat) to Jersey (St Aubin's Bay). Mother's calm.

**CH IX:** Jersey: Cousin Marianne (sister of Mr George Corbet, rector); Cousin George (rector, white hair); cousins Katherine, Paulina, Eleanor (kind nurse), two little boys (twins; mother died). Vevette ill (long fever/swoon); spring; learns March.

**CH X:** Pierre Le Febre settles in Jersey. Blanchon given to Eleanor. Voyage to London; uncle Charles & aunt "Jem" (Jemima; fine lady, patches, great wig). Mr Samuel Pepys (wife black, French-speaking) buys jewels. Vevette tempted by London. Aunt Jem's "Puritanism". Simon & Jeanne found at Threadneedle Street French church. Andrew arranges Cornwall posting.

**CH XI:** Tre Madoc (Cornwall). Andrew's mother (Aunt Amy), sisters Betty (small, dark, mischievous), Margaret/Meg (tall, fair, school), Rosamond (studious, bookish). Chevalier father's gold. Mother's failing health. Mrs Deborah (housekeeper, Presbyterian). Dame school: Peggy Mellish.

**CH XII:** Deborah & Jeanne quarrel (salad, pig). Jeanne's room haunted (headless woman, fiery eyes). Vevette & Andrew (hare's-foot; hawks). The Well House (St Wenna's Well; Dinah, foundling "Diane", black hair, fairy-seeming; East Country family). Mother proposes buying Well House. Betty & Mr Lovel secret meetings at Torden's cottage (Rosamond saw figures).

**CH XIII:** Dryden's poems book from Aunt Jem; Betty takes it; Andrew's suspicion; Vevette confesses lie to mother; Rosamond's sincerity; Meg gossip. Vevette and Betty quarrel.

**CH XIV:** Move to Well House. Dinah (waiting-gentlewoman; Vaudois "Noble Lesson"; gold dove). Lois Barker (lame; Vevette teaches reading). Betty & Lovel exposed at Torden's cottage (Vevette accused; Andrew doubts). Mother breaks engagement. Betty marries Lovel. Lord Stanton (Stanton Court, Devon) visits; receives inheritance-property exchange; Vevette's guardian. Andrew leaves for voyage (ship *Enterprise*, West Indies).

**CH XV:** Stanton Court. Lady Stanton (stepmother); Lord Stanton (choleric, kind). Martha (stepdaughter, cold), Theo (second daughter, warm; later marries Dean of Exeter). Captain Bernard (Martha's husband; Mrs Bernard). Mother dies suddenly (heart/faint) at Stanton Court. Vevette made school-mistress via Dinah. Lewis Stanton (son, "young lord"; angles for Vevette). Vevette refuses Basil Champernoun. Vevette goes to London.

**CH XVI:** Exeter; Lady Jemima (Theo's godmother). London with Uncle Charles (gaming, debts) and Aunt Jem (Jemima; fine lady, wig, patches; Mercer maid; Mr Goodgroome music master). Mr Pepys. Lady Castlemaine; Mrs Godolphin. Vevette sees a "ghost" (father-like French officer) at French ambassador's party; this is Marquis de Fayrolles (father's eldest brother).

**CH XVII:** Madame Zenobie (Aunt Zenobie, Madame de Fayrolles) and Monsieur de Fayrolles (Uncle, Catholic convert); Father Martien (Jesuit; Italian/Florentine-educated). Aunt Jem dies. Andrew reported married to a Jamaica heiress (false). Andrew letter/news; Aunt Jem's death-bed.

**CH XVIII:** Mercer declines to go to France (goes to sister's school in Hackney). Vevette goes to Paris via Calais; sees oppression (vineyard; Marquis hunting). Conversion (in king's chapel). Illness; regrets.

**CH XIX:** Paris winter; Uncle's disgrace (Madame de Montespan's enmity). Uncle questions Vevette about father's hidden treasure (Tour d'Antin vault). Uncle declares Vevette illegitimate. Monsieur de Luynes proposes; Vevette refuses; locked in attic with gray cat.

**CH XX:** Journey to Marseilles, "You shall have no choice". Aunt rails. Uncle strikes old preacher Monsieur Morin; Vevette rebukes uncle. David Sablot (overseer at convent) given Gospel of St Luke; Vevette's note to Lord Stanton. Ursuline convent (Mother Superior; Mother Mary of the Incarnation; Sister St Stanislaus, who knew Lucille; Sister Joanne). Destination: New France (Canada) bride ship.

**CH XXI:** Convent life; Desirée (orphan; died later at sea); Louisonne; Mademoiselle de Troyon. Sister St Stanislaus's tale: Lucille drowned (lost clothing on bush by river) — later revealed false. Mother Mary's rebuke.

**CH XXII:** Voyage on bride ship, storms, Desirée dies; British ship *Good Hope* (Captain Mayhew, Boston). Vevette meets Andrew (Captain Mayhew's ship; Andrew was passenger). Married by Rev. Mr Norton at sea (Church of England). Boston: Mr Folsom; Mrs Folsom. Mother Mary sent to French ship.

**CH XXIII (Conclusion):** Lucille found alive at Boston (interpreter; escaped convent). Lived in New England 6 years (Hampton). Father Martien seen with Indian raiders. Return to Cornwall; Aunt Amy; David in Penzance (married Cornish maid); Lucille with Vevette; Jeanne & Simon long lived. Fates: Betty ("nothing said"); Uncle Charles's wife Felicia; Monsieur de Fayrolles killed in duel; Susanne milliner in London; Lord & Lady Stanton; Lewis married Provençal; Theo (Dean's wife, no children); Margaret 20 grandchildren; Rosamond divides time. Closing texts: James 1:8 (double-minded), 1 John 2:15, Matt 6:24. Signed Agnes Genevieve Corbet née d'Antin.

**Publisher catalogue:** John F. Shaw & Co., 48 Paternoster Row; Guernsey titles (Through Unknown Ways, Oldham, Loveday's History, Foster Sisters, Lady Betty's Governess, Lady Rosamond's Book, Winifred); Rev. Andrew Reed titles.
